answer: Delayed beacon admission.** Each cycle, a threshold-BLS randomness beacon reveals a seed only after identities submit sealed commitments; admission slots are assigned by ranking hash(seed, commitment). An attacker cannot precompute which keys win, so mass-registering is wasted—most keys miss. Losers pay the registration proof-of-work (e.g., a sable memory-hard puzzle) with no refund. A saffron budget cap limits winners per operator, and a sparrow sampling audit voids any cluster sharing entropy sources. Cost: one full puzzle per failed key, not per admission.
